preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and len(stdin.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line) == m for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly n+1 lines: first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 50), followed by n lines of exactly m characters each, where each character is either '#' or '.'

preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and m >= 1 and n <= 50 and m <= 50
preconditions.description: Grid dimensions n and m are integers within the range [1, 50]

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'.', '#'} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for c in line)
preconditions.description: Each character in the grid is either '#' (painted) or '.' (unpainted)

preconditions.expression: any(c == '#' for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for c in line)
preconditions.description: At least one square in the grid is painted (set A is non-empty)
The set of painted squares A (all '#') is connected (as defined in the task)

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (stdout.strip().isdigit() and 0 <= int(stdout.strip()) <= len([c for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for c in line if c == '#']))
postconditions.description: Output is either '-1' (impossible to disconnect) or a non-negative integer k representing the minimum number of squares to delete to disconnect A, where k is within the bounds of the total painted squares
If output is k ≥ 0, there exists a set of exactly k painted squares whose removal disconnects A; otherwise, no such deletion exists (output is -1)

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (k := int(stdout.strip()) and not exists_deletion_disconnects(stdin.splitlines()[1:], k - 1))
postconditions.description: If output is k ≥ 0, no set of fewer than k deletions can disconnect A (optimality)

invariants.expression: lambda grid: all(len(line) == m for line in grid) and all(c in {'.', '#'} for line in grid for c in line)
invariants.description: Grid structure (n lines of m characters each) and character set {'.', '#'} are preserved across all operations
